prerequisites: Basic skills in computing, programming, and system administration
Written and oral communication skills in English

learning_outcomes.text: Analyze technological evolutions in ICT considering their social and environmental impacts.
Identify relevant emerging technologies (GAI, IoT, Big Data) to address industrial or territorial challenges.
Understand and design digital solutions while accounting for digital sobriety, data protection, and sustainability constraints.
Understand the evolution of information and communication technologies (ICT) and their innovation dynamics.
Know the key concepts related to distributed architectures, Internet of Things, Generative AI, and information systems.
Be aware of legal, ethical, and environmental challenges in digital uses (GDPR, digital sobriety, data sovereignty).
Identify and analyze current ICT use cases in industrial, territorial, and civic contexts.
Be able to use basic tools (APIs, open data, web visualization) to experiment with technical scenarios.
Be aware of the impacts of digital technologies on individuals, organizations, and the environment.
Develop a reflective stance on the responsible and reasoned use of emerging technologies.

syllabus_topics: Chapter 1: Introduction to trends and disruptions in ICT
1.1 Evolution of technologies and societies: from writing to artificial intelligence
1.2 Technological acceleration, singularity and ecological transition
Chapter 2: Major families of emerging technologies
2.1 Internet of Things, Big Data, distributed systems
2.2 Artificial intelligence: history, typologies, societal and environmental issues
Chapter 3: Communications between systems and cyber-physical paradigms
3.1 Network protocols (TCP/IP, OSI model), CPS and digital twins
3.2 Observation and tracing of exchanges (Wireshark)
Chapter 4: From static web to dynamic web
4.1 HTML, CSS, JS: basic structure of a personal site (CV)
4.2 Simple web servers and client-server exchanges
Chapter 5: REST APIs and open data
5.1 API operation, JSON format, HTTP call
5.2 Cartography and open data (OpenStreetMap, geo.api.gouv.fr, etc.)
Chapter 6: Creative engineering and preparation for presentation
6.1 Problem decomposition, reasoned use of GAI in projects
6.2 Synthetic presentation in English, evaluation criteria and self-assessment
HTML/CSS structure of a CV page, simple client-server interaction, REST API call
Presentation of topics, team formation, project theme selection
Project progress monitoring through supervised iterations (technical and reflective coaching)
Individual or pair experiments: technical implementation of solutions (web, GAI, data, HMI)
Final project presentations in English with peer evaluation and self-assessment
teaching_methods: Lectures: theoretical input and contextualization of current trends, in an interactive and reflective format that encourages discussion.
Tutorials (TD): hands-on application through practical exercises.

Capstone group project: collaborative work on a complex, initially unfamiliar topic, using a problem decomposition approach. Intensive use of generative AI tools, with a critical evaluation of their pedagogical contribution.
assessment_rules: The evaluation formula is (1*DS1+1*PJ1)/2. Assessment is a combination of self-assessment and peer evaluation, focusing on the ability to convey the knowledge acquired and applied.
degree: Titre d'ingénieur ENIT (cycle ingénieur, semestres 5-10; orientación mecánica/producción)
